system.name: Sundial
system.one_liner: A family of time series foundation models that predict the next patch's distribution with a flow-matching TimeFlow loss on continuous patch tokens.

content.variant_note: two-level contrast: native vs foreign tokenization on top, three numbered model designs below with the proposed one last
content.argues: Sundial is the first time series foundation model family that is both native (continuous tokens) and flexible (generative loss, no prior distribution).
content.subject: Time series data from seven domains tokenized two ways, and three model designs that differ in token type and training loss.

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw competing designs as columns with one shared skeleton so that only the differing parts (token colour, loss box, background tint) change, give each design axis its own colour channel with a legend in the section heading, and mark the proposed column with a red title.
lessons.suits: Positioning a new model inside a small design space, for example foundation models that differ by tokenization and training objective.

evidence: A native time series model operates on the original series of continuous values.
A flexible foundation model is pre-trained without specifying prior distributions.
Sundial is the first family of native and flexible time series foundation models.

summary: Sundial is a family of time series foundation models that predict the next patch's distribution with a flow-matching TimeFlow loss and no discrete tokenization. Figure 1 is a two-band motivation figure in a single column. The upper band shows series from seven domains (a blue strip of white line icons) and contrasts native continuous patch tokens (overlaid curves cut into boxes) with foreign discrete tokens (numbers turned into integer chips). The lower band lines up three numbered designs with the same token, model, token, loss skeleton: parametric densities with a Prior Loss, language modeling with cross-entropy, and Sundial with TimeFlow. Chip colour marks token type, background tint marks specific versus flexible, and Sundial gets a red title.
summary_zh: Sundial 是一族时间序列基础模型，用流匹配的 TimeFlow 损失预测下一段连续补丁的分布。图一分两层：上层对比连续（原生）与离散（外来）分词，下层并排三种设计，仅损失与词元颜色不同，红色标题的 Sundial 是新方案。
notes: Prior side-by-side-contrast kept; stage-pipeline added for the token, model, token, loss chains inside each column. Panels counted as five (two tokenization panels and three design columns). Token colours in column 1 are read as blue chips under the pink tint (from the overlay opacities in the digest). The domain icons are unlabelled, so their meanings are guesses from their shapes.
